note: Deviations from the frozen BASELINE / mapping rules, with their resolutions. BASELINE.json itself is never modified.

deviations.baseline_reason: condvar_multiple_locks: one condvar waited on with two mutexes
deviations.action: The original structure is inexpressible in the DSL (a condvar is bound to one mutex; `lock m2 { cv.wait(); }` for a cv bound to m1 is S104). The original task was moved under `boundary/` as a negative example (direct.skel -> S104, gold.cir.json -> UNSUPPORTED), and the subset skeleton was promoted to the new task `condvar/two_cv_two_locks` (recorded in BASELINE_EXT.json; not claimed equivalent to the frozen baseline).

resolution.summary: Original task moved to boundary/same_cv_different_locks (SKEL reports S104, CIR reports UNSUPPORTED); the subset skeleton became the separate task condvar/two_cv_two_locks, explicitly not equivalent to the baseline.

deviations.reason: ConcIR a35dc86 classifies seq_hole as UNSUPPORTED in the precise backend. Emitting seq_hole would make every skeleton containing a compute hole UNSUPPORTED, so no PASS baseline could be reproduced.
deviations.mitigation: compute lowers to the semantics-neutral nop; the source-map construct is `compute`. The front-end rejects compute footprints that name a shared resource (S110), so a hole can only read/write locals and nop is a sound abstraction for synchronization semantics. The cost is that a hole's effect on local data is invisible in the model.

resolution.summary: compute stays mapped to nop; the source-map construct is renamed to compute; S110 guarantees the reads/writes footprint contains only local variables.

deviations.reason: The plan's `extern fn compute();` uses `compute`, which is a DSL keyword (the compute hole). The sequential helper is named `helper` in gold.skel; the contract does not reference the helper by name, so verification is unaffected.

resolution.summary: accepted: contract does not reference the helper name
